No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of install-time or interpreter-startup execution via .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py/PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.

The VM creation, SSH/rsync, code-server installation, AWS/ECR calls, and remote command execution in plato/cli/chronos/dev/runner.py appear to be user-invoked development CLI behavior for chronos dev, not automatic execution during installation or import.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential theft: no confirmed evidence. References to PLATO_API_KEY, AWS STS/ECR, and SSH key paths appear within user-invoked CLI/VM provisioning flows. There is no evidence of broad environment-variable harvesting, home-directory/.env/SSH key/cloud credential discovery, or coupling with external exfiltration.
  • Exfiltration/staging: no confirmed malicious evidence. base64 is used to write configuration files to a remote VM in chunks; there is no evidence of archiving harvested files or uploading them to attacker-controlled endpoints.
  • Persistence: no confirmed evidence. StartupProfiler and Startup Timing are performance-profiling names, not cron/systemd/launch-agent/shell-profile persistence mechanisms.
  • Lateral movement: no confirmed malicious evidence. Remote VM, ECR, SSH, and rsync usage appears to support development/simulator execution. Patterns such as CI token theft, Kubernetes service-account abuse, or Docker socket takeover were not identified in the provided text.
  • Stealth/loaders: no confirmed malicious evidence. The base64 usage in the provided text supports configuration transfer, and there is no evidence tying obfuscation, downloader stubs, or exec/eval-style staged loaders to malicious behavior.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

Based on the provided text, there is no confirmed evidence of hidden payloads in the PyPI artifact, unexplained native binaries, sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting, or wheel/sdist behavior mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The package contains 931 files, but only selected files were provided in the text corpus; unprovided files should be checked for automatic execution hooks or hidden payloads.
  • Only the sdist is shown, so wheel-vs-sdist behavioral differences were not assessed.
